```{r}
library(dplyr)

blca_obj <- readRDS("../../results/rds/blca_obj.rds")

count_tbl <- function(x) {
  out <- as.data.frame(table(x), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  colnames(out) <- c("Class", "Cells")
  out <- out %>% arrange(desc(Cells))
  out$Share <- sprintf("%.1f%%", out$Cells / sum(out$Cells) * 100)
  out
}

cell_type_tbl <- count_tbl(blca_obj$Cell_Type_2)
condition_tbl <- count_tbl(blca_obj$Condition)

cellchat_cell_types <- levels(blca_obj$Cell_Type_2) %>%
  grep("Cycling", ., invert = TRUE, value = TRUE) %>%
  setdiff(c("Adipocyte", "Schwann", "Smooth_Muscle", "Others"))
cellchat_cell_tbl <- count_tbl(blca_obj$Cell_Type_2[blca_obj$Cell_Type_2 %in% cellchat_cell_types])

total_cells <- ncol(blca_obj)
```

## Overview

This report summarizes the CellChat-based communication analysis implemented in `code/04.Communication.R` and narrows the presentation to two pathways of interest: PD-L1 and IGF signaling. The full analysis in the script computes a global cell-cell interaction network, global communication patterns, and pathway-level networks; here I keep the report focused on the pathway outputs that best support biological interpretation.

The integrated BLCA object contains `r total_cells` cells. Its annotation structure provides the cellular context for the communication model:

`r knitr::kable(cell_type_tbl, align = c("l", "r", "r"))`

The CellChat model does not use every `cell_type_2` label. In the script, cycling populations and a small set of rare or less informative lineages are excluded before inference, leaving the following communication input set:

`r knitr::kable(cellchat_cell_tbl, align = c("l", "r", "r"))`

The excluded labels are `Cycling`, `Adipocyte`, `Schwann`, `Smooth_Muscle`, and `Others`.

Condition balance is also preserved in the integrated object and is important for interpreting the perturbation-specific communication patterns:

`r knitr::kable(condition_tbl, align = c("l", "r", "r"))`

## PD-L1 signaling

PD-L1 is one of the most interesting immune-evasion-related pathways in the CellChat output. The pathway-level views below show how PD-L1 signaling is distributed across sender and receiver cell types, where the strongest connections appear, and which cell types dominate the outgoing or incoming roles.

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Circle.Network.Pathway.PD-L1.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Heatmap.Pathway.PD-L1.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Chord.Pathway.PD-L1.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Heatmap_signalingRole.PD-L1.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Bar.LR_Contribution.PD-L1.png" width="100%">

Together, these figures indicate how PD-L1-related communication is organized at the network level rather than being restricted to a single isolated pair of populations. That makes PD-L1 a useful readout for identifying cell states that may contribute to local immune suppression in the BLCA microenvironment.

## IGF signaling

The IGF axis is the second pathway I keep in the report because it captures a growth-factor program that is often linked to stromal support, survival, and tumor-associated remodeling. In the CellChat output, the IGF pathway also shows a clear, structured communication architecture across the major cell groups.

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Circle.Network.Pathway.IGF.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Heatmap.Pathway.IGF.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Chord.Pathway.IGF.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Heatmap_signalingRole.IGF.png" width="100%">

<img src="assets/04.Conmmunication/Pathway_Level/Bar.LR_Contribution.IGF.png" width="100%">

The IGF pathway is especially useful for contrasting with PD-L1 because it reflects a growth and survival axis rather than an immune checkpoint axis. Reading the two together helps separate suppressive immune communication from stromal or proliferative signaling.

## Takeaway

The communication analysis supports two complementary conclusions. First, the global CellChat network shows that intercellular signaling in BLCA is organized and cell-type specific rather than diffuse. Second, the PD-L1 and IGF pathway panels isolate two biologically distinct communication modes: one linked to immune regulation and one linked to growth-factor signaling. Keeping the report focused on these two axes makes the pathway interpretation clearer than presenting the full set of CellChat pathways.
